definition: A random variable is a variable whose possible values are numerical outcomes of a random phenomenon.
details: A random variable is a variable whose possible values are numerical outcomes of a random phenomenon. There are two types of random variables: discrete and continuous.

explainer.lead: A random variable assigns numerical values to the outcomes of a random phenomenon, letting probability be handled with numbers. It matters because it turns uncertain events into quantities that can be modelled and computed with.

tiers.eli5: Think of rolling a die and writing down the number you get: the roll is random, but the number is a value you can work with.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use random variables to model noise, uncertainty and sampled data in probabilistic models; a common pitfall is confusing a discrete variable with a continuous one and applying the wrong distribution or summation.
tiers.paperLevel: A random variable is a variable whose possible values are numerical outcomes of a random phenomenon; the two types are discrete (countable outcomes) and continuous (outcomes over a continuum).

explainer.example: The number of heads in 10 coin flips is a discrete random variable taking values 0 to 10.
